prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1336; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Can you confirm you're comfortable with us recording this call?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving south on the main road in League City, near one of the shopping centers. It was late afternoon and traffic was fairly light.

Q: What were the weather and road conditions like?

A: It was clear and dry. Nothing unusual about the road that I noticed.

Q: Tell me what happened in your own words.

A: The other car crossed into my lane. I tried to swerve right, but there wasn't much room, and we ended up hitting nose to nose. It didn't feel like a high-speed impact, though. I'd guess we were both going maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour.

Q: Did your airbags deploy?

A: Yes, both the driver and passenger airbags came out.

Q: Did you feel any pain or injuries right after the collision?

A: My left wrist hurt right away. I was holding the steering wheel and it jammed. I didn't think much of it at first, but it got worse over the next hour.

Q: Did you seek medical treatment?

A: Yes. An ambulance took me to the emergency room, and they did X-rays. The doctor said I had a fracture in my wrist and I'd need a cast and follow-up with a specialist.

Q: Were you able to get out of the vehicle on your own?

A: Yes, I got out on my own. I was shaken up but I could walk.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the collision?

A: Only that I've been trying to keep track of my medical bills and I'm dealing with some time off work. I'm happy to send over the records.

Q: Thank you. We'll follow up with you about those documents. That concludes the statement.

A: Okay, thank you.
